draft.title: Nutrition and hydration for performance
card: Carbohydrate
Carbohydrate is stored in the muscles and liver as glycogen. Eating it before and during longer exercise keeps fuel available, and eating it afterwards refills the stores.
Protein
Protein supplies amino acids, which the body uses to repair and rebuild muscle. It is most useful after exercise, when muscle has been stressed.
Water
Sweat loses water, and a fluid loss that is not replaced can make exercise feel harder and lower performance. Drinking before, during and after exercise helps keep fluid levels steady.
Used well, these nutrients help an athlete perform for longer, delay fatigue and recover for the next session.
draft.remember: Carbohydrate refuels, protein repairs and water replaces lost fluid, so athletes plan all three around training.

a.q: Which choice best matches a nutrient to its main job after hard exercise?
opts: Protein, to repair and rebuild muscle tissue
Carbohydrate, to repair and rebuild muscle tissue
Water, to refill glycogen stores in the muscles
Protein, to replace the fluid lost through sweat
a.why: Protein supplies amino acids, which the body uses to repair muscle. Carbohydrate is the nutrient that refills glycogen stores, so it is the tempting swap, but it does not supply the amino acids used for repair.
a.clue: Amino acids are used to rebuild muscle.

b.q: Priya plays a 90 minute netball tournament match in warm weather. She eats carbohydrate and sips water at breaks. Why does this help her performance late in the match?
opts: It keeps fuel and fluid supplied, which delays fatigue
It repairs muscle damage as the match is played
It removes the need for fuel from her stored glycogen
It replaces sweat loss only, so fuel is not affected
b.why: Carbohydrate keeps fuel available and water replaces sweat, so both help delay fatigue. Repair is mostly a job for protein after exercise, so the muscle repair option is tempting but does not fit what Priya is doing during the match.
b.clue: Think about what carbohydrate and water each supply during play.

a.best: Protein, to repair and rebuild muscle tissue

b.best: It keeps fuel and fluid supplied, which delays fatigue

problems.detail: A netball match is 60 minutes of play (four 15-minute quarters), and tournament matches are often shorter, so a '90 minute netball tournament match' is unrealistic. Use a different sport or a realistic duration.
The distractor 'It replaces sweat loss only, so fuel is not affected' uses 'only', an absolute the card does not use. It makes the option easy to rule out without knowing the idea.
